cases.title: Born on the Fourth of July

evidenceReconstruction.sourceOverview: Paralyzed in the Vietnam war, Ron Kovic becomes an anti-war and pro-human rights political activist after feeling betrayed by the country he fought for.

allowedSourceMaterial.overview: Paralyzed in the Vietnam war, Ron Kovic becomes an anti-war and pro-human rights political activist after feeling betrayed by the country he fought for.

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: When the patriotic ideals he fought for collapse upon his return home, how does one veteran channel deep betrayal into national defiance?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: Paralyzed during the Vietnam War, Ron Kovic returns home to face profound physical trauma, rising disillusionment, and a nation that leaves him feeling betrayed by the cause he served.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Heavy, thoughtful, and deliberately paced, offering an emotionally demanding drama best experienced with focused attention.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Oliver Stone directs a weighty biographical drama that transforms personal sacrifice and wartime trauma into a passionate awakening for civil rights and peace.

humanGroundTruth.acceptedAdjudicationRationale: Director "Oliver Stone" and runtime "145 minutes" match exactly, and the Description and Curiosity hook accurately reflect the authorized overview (paralysis in Vietnam, disillusionment, feeling betrayed by his country). However, the Why-watch field states Kovic's activism becomes "a passionate awakening for civil rights and peace" — the authorized overview specifically states he becomes an "anti-war and pro-human rights" activist. "Civil rights" is a distinct political cause (typically referring to domestic racial/social equality movements) from "human rights," and substituting one for the other materially mischaracterizes the authorized fact. Recommend correcting "civil rights" to "human rights" to match the authorized overview precisely.

verifierExecution.lowRiskCoverageSummaryRationale: All factual claims, character arcs, and directorial attributions across description, whyWatch, curiosityHook, and vibeSummary are fully grounded in the authorized overview, packet metadata, and semantic classifications.

observedDefectPattern.authorizedCounterpart: anti-war and pro-human rights political activist (overview)
observedDefectPattern.observedDefectSummary: The editorial copy states Kovic's activism becomes "a passionate awakening for civil rights and peace", whereas the authorized overview specifically states he becomes an "anti-war and pro-human rights" activist. "Civil rights" (domestic constitutional/social equality) is a distinct political cause from universal "human rights".

hypothesizedVerifierMissMechanism.mechanismRationale: The verifier output rationale stated that all factual claims and character arcs were fully grounded in the overview. A plausible development hypothesis is that the verifier evaluated "civil rights" and "human rights" as semantically equivalent progressive activist causes. The frozen outputs do not establish whether the miss arose from representation-level synonymy, decision thresholding, or another internal factor.

evidenceReconstruction.sourceOverview: Teenager Cleo's school science project goes quite awry, causing her popular older sister Molly to go invisible.

allowedSourceMaterial.overview: Teenager Cleo's school science project goes quite awry, causing her popular older sister Molly to go invisible.

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: With a high school routine to maintain and an unintended vanish, how long can two very different sisters keep an invisible reality under wraps?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: When teen Cleo's school science experiment spirals out of control, the unexpected fallout leaves her popular older sister Molly completely invisible, sparking a frantic scramble to navigate everyday life.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Light, energetic fantasy-comedy with an easygoing rhythm that fits a lively movie night with family or friends.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Directed by Paul Hoen, this brisk 78-minute fantasy-comedy offers an easy, fast-paced family adventure shaped by lighthearted mishap and playful sisterly chaos.

humanGroundTruth.acceptedAdjudicationRationale: Director "Paul Hoen" and runtime "78 minutes" both match the authorized basis exactly, and the Description accurately restates the overview (Cleo's science project, Molly's invisibility). However, the Curiosity hook introduces a specific plot mechanism/goal — that the sisters are trying to "keep an invisible reality under wraps" (i.e., conceal Molly's condition from others) — which is not stated anywhere in the authorized overview. The source only establishes the setup (the experiment causes invisibility); it says nothing about secrecy, concealment, or a "maintain the routine while hiding it" structure. This is an invented narrative mechanism presented as fact. Recommend revising the hook to focus on the stated setup (adjusting to sudden invisibility) without asserting a concealment plot that isn't authorized.

verifierExecution.lowRiskCoverageSummaryRationale: All editorial claims in the visible copy remain strictly grounded in the authorized overview, packet facts (director Paul Hoen, 78-minute runtime, genres Comedy/Fantasy/Adventure), and accepted semantic classifications without introducing ungrounded story mechanisms, real-world lore, or spoiler reveals.

evidenceReconstruction.sourceOverview: One part vigilante, one part criminal kingpin, Red Hood begins cleaning up Gotham with the efficiency of Batman, but without following the same ethical code.

allowedSourceMaterial.overview: One part vigilante, one part criminal kingpin, Red Hood begins cleaning up Gotham with the efficiency of Batman, but without following the same ethical code.

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: When a ruthless kingpin wages war on Gotham's streets under Batman's tactical mold, what line separates the vigilante from the criminal?

However, the Description refers to "the Dark Knight's strict moral restraints" — "Dark Knight" is an unstated epithet/nickname for Batman drawn from broader franchise lore/branding, not from the authorized overview, which names him only as "Batman." Recommend replacing "the Dark Knight's" with "Batman's" to stay strictly within the authorized text.

verifierExecution.lowRiskCoverageSummaryRationale: All editorial claims strictly adhere to authorized source packet boundaries: the 75-minute runtime matches facts.runtimeMinutes; genres (Animation, Crime, Mystery) are faithfully represented; plot references to Red Hood cleaning up Gotham with Batman's efficiency without his ethical code accurately reflect the synopsis; no external franchise lore or hidden identity spoilers are introduced; and tone/viewing attributes align directly with accepted semantic classifications.

allowedSourceMaterial.overview: Daigo, a cellist, is laid off from his orchestra and moves with his wife back to his small hometown where the living is cheaper. visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: Expecting a routine desk job, an unemployed musician inadvertently steps into the solemn, intimate world of preparing the deceased for their final journey.
visibleEditorialCopy.description: After his orchestra disbands, cellist Daigo returns with his wife to his small hometown. Looking for steady work, an interview for what seems like a travel agency instead places him as an assistant to an undertaker.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: A slow, thoughtful Japanese drama with heavy emotional weight, rewarding patient and engaged viewing.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Directed by Yojiro Takita, this reflective drama handles grief and vocation with quiet tenderness, finding unexpected dignity in the delicate rituals of saying goodbye.

humanGroundTruth.acceptedAdjudicationRationale: Director "Yojiro Takita" and country "Japan" match exactly, and most of the copy accurately reflects the authorized overview (return to hometown, mistaken travel agency interview, actual work as an undertaker's assistant). However, the Description states "After his orchestra disbands" — the authorized overview specifies Daigo "is laid off from his orchestra," which describes his personal job loss, not the dissolution of the orchestra itself. These are materially different facts (individual termination vs. organizational collapse), and the substitution misrepresents the authorized premise. Recommend correcting to reflect that Daigo was laid off/let go, not that the orchestra disbanded.

verifierExecution.lowRiskCoverageSummaryRationale: All visible editorial copy strictly adheres to authorized packet facts, the accepted semantic classification, and setup story material. The director attribution, country/genre descriptor ('Japanese drama'), plot premise of an unemployed cellist becoming an undertaker's assistant, and experiential tone are fully authorized without crossing spoiler boundaries or introducing external lore.

cases.title: Nothing Left to Do But Cry

evidenceReconstruction.sourceOverview: Two 20th-century friends accidentally stumble into the year 1492, where they meet a charming teen and try to alter history.

allowedSourceMaterial.overview: Two 20th-century friends accidentally stumble into the year 1492, where they meet a charming teen and try to alter history.

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: Stranded centuries before their own era, can these two ordinary companions actually change the course of history without unraveling their own path?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: Two twentieth-century friends suddenly find themselves displaced into the year 1492, navigating an unfamiliar era while meeting a charming local teen and hatching a bold plan to meddle with history.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Light and funny fantasy comedy with a steady pace, engaging historical confusion, and an easygoing spirit ideal for watching with friends.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Directed by Roberto Benigni and Massimo Troisi, this Italian comedy blends playful fantasy and historical misadventure into an inventive, lighthearted time-travel romp.

humanGroundTruth.acceptedAdjudicationRationale: Director attribution "Roberto Benigni & Massimo Troisi" matches exactly. Description and Why-watch stay faithfully within the authorized overview (accidental time-slip to 1492, meeting a charming teen, attempting to alter history). However, the Curiosity hook adds "without unraveling their own path" — this invokes a specific time-travel-paradox stake (risk to their own timeline/existence) that is not stated anywhere in the authorized overview, which only says they "try to alter history." This is a genre-trope assumption imported from general time-travel-film conventions rather than the authorized source, and should be revised to a hook grounded only in the stated "alter history" premise (e.g., focusing on the culture-clash or the stakes of tampering with the past generally, without the paradox-to-self implication).

verifierExecution.lowRiskCoverageSummaryRationale: All visible editorial copy strictly adheres to authorized sources: metadata facts (directors Benigni and Troisi, Italian production context, Comedy/Fantasy genres), allowed synopsis setup (two 20th-century friends stumbling into 1492, meeting a teen, attempting to alter history), and accepted semantic classifications (light/funny tone, steady pace, engaged attention, friend-viewing situation). No ungrounded plot mechanisms, external lore, deadlines, or spoiler boundaries are violated.

observedDefectPattern.authorizedCounterpart: Two 20th-century friends accidentally stumble into the year 1492, where they meet a charming teen and try to alter history (overview)
observedDefectPattern.observedDefectSummary: The curiosityHook adds "without unraveling their own path", invoking a specific time-travel paradox consequence/stake not stated anywhere in the authorized overview, which specifies only that they "try to alter history".

hypothesizedVerifierMissMechanism.mechanismRationale: The verifier output rationale found that no ungrounded plot mechanisms were violated. A plausible development hypothesis is that the verifier treated the paradox clause as standard rhetorical tension or generic genre framing common to time-travel stories, rather than an ungrounded narrative rule. The frozen evidence does not establish whether the model evaluated the paradox clause as a concrete mechanism.

recoverabilityAnalysis.recoverabilityRationale: The discrepancy between the visible editorial copy and the authorized source packet is directly observable by comparing the supplied source packet and editorial copy on existing text surfaces.

repeatedLinguisticAndSemanticPatterns: Interrogative Hook Premise Inflation (4/7): Writers introduce ungrounded plot goals (concealment in Invisible Sister), micro-settings (cockpit in 7500), temporal magnifications (decades in Guardians), or sci-fi genre stakes (timeline paradox in Nothing Left to Do But Cry) inside curiosityHook questions. The verifier output rationale in each case treated curiosityHook framing as grounded in setup material.

Synonym and Cause Substitution (2/7): Writers substituted distinct concepts for authorized terms ("civil rights" for "human rights" in Born on the Fourth of July; "orchestra disbands" for "laid off from his orchestra" in Departures). The verifier accepted both as authorized without issue flags.
Alias and External Lore Import (1/7): In Batman: Under the Red Hood, the writer imported "the Dark Knight", which the verifier did not flag despite explicitly auditing for external lore.
crossCasePatterns.subtleInferenceVsExplicitUnsupportedness: All seven misses cluster around subtle source-boundary overextensions, narrative premise sharpening, or entity substitutions on otherwise well-grounded editorial copy, rather than gross hallucinations of nonexistent entities. In all cases, the factual defect is directly identifiable by comparing the editorial copy to the authorized source packet.
crossCasePatterns.verifierMissMechanismsEpistemicStatus: The frozen outputs do not allow us to determine whether misses arose from pretraining memory, semantic similarity tolerances, genre priors, decision thresholding, or other internal mechanisms. All verifier miss mechanism classifications in this taxonomy are labeled INFERENTIAL_DEVELOPMENT_HYPOTHESIS.

interventionHypotheses.promptClarification: PLAUSIBLE_BUT_UNTESTED. Stricter prompt instructions on interrogative hook premises, exact alias prohibition, and duration/entity precision are development hypotheses that require independent empirical testing.
interventionHypotheses.structuredDecisionRule: PLAUSIBLE_BUT_UNTESTED. Explicit span-level evidence pointers across all fields are plausible but have not been evaluated in this experiment.
interventionHypotheses.newEvidenceFields: NOT_INDICATED_BY_CURRENT_FAILURE_ANALYSIS. All seven discrepancies are directly observable on existing input packet surfaces.
interventionHypotheses.schemaChanges: NOT_INDICATED_BY_CURRENT_FAILURE_ANALYSIS. Existing risk categories already encompass all seven defect types.
interventionHypotheses.humanReviewBoundary: Human review remains the definitive ground truth for subtle boundary distinctions.

developmentLeakageBoundary.policy: These exact seven candidate records are formally classified as DEVELOPMENT_EXPOSED. Future tuning examples must be synthetic or separately sourced, and future semantic evaluation must be conducted on an independent dataset.
